regulation_content.regmate_comment: Two things a practitioner should register here. First, the MGA route has been taken out — the definitions of 'Managing General Agent' and 'binding agreement', and the MGA limb of 'Applicant', were omitted w.e.f. 12 June 2026 when the Managing General Agents Regulations, 2026 moved MGAs into their own regime. regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 5 (source p.5)
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the eligibility conditions for registration, which differ by the applicant's structure — an Indian insurer/re-insurer setting up an unincorporated place of business; a foreign insurer/re-insurer or Lloyd's setting up a branch; an IRDAI-registered branch office of a foreign insurer or Lloyd's India; a public company or wholly-owned subsidiary; an insurance co-operative society; or an overseas body corporate. Common threads include an IRDAI or home-regulator NOC, a satisfactory compliance track record, board undertakings on capital, solvency and liabilities, FATF-compliant jurisdiction, and fit-and-proper key persons.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The eligibility test is structure-driven, so the first move is always to classify the applicant correctly — the conditions for an Indian insurer's place of business are not those for a foreign re-insurer's branch. For foreign applicants, two conditions are easy to under-plan: the DTAA-jurisdiction requirement and the minimum credit rating held for the last three years. The MGA limb of this regulation was omitted w.e.f. 12 June 2026.
regulation_content.practical_point: Classify the applicant against the correct sub-regulation, then build the evidence file for that limb — NOC, home-regulator registration, three-year credit rating, DTAA status, board undertakings and the Regulation 17(7) reporting structure. Do not mix conditions across applicant types.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Assemble and retain the applicant-specific eligibility evidence — NOCs, regulatory status, credit rating, DTAA confirmation, board undertakings and fit-and-proper records — before filing.
regulation_content.example: A foreign re-insurer setting up a branch IIO must show a home-regulator NOC, a three-year track record of at least good financial-security credit rating, DTAA-jurisdiction status, and NOF compliance under Section 6(3) of the Insurance Act, 1938.
regulation_content.risk_point: Applications most often stall on the foreign-applicant conditions — a credit rating short of three years, or incorporation in a non-DTAA jurisdiction. Board undertakings that are generic rather than specific to capital, solvency and liabilities are another common gap.
regulation_content.interview_point: A practical interview question: walk through the eligibility conditions you would test for a foreign re-insurer wanting a GIFT IFSC branch, and identify which two conditions foreign applicants most often fail.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Home-regulator/IRDAI NOC; satisfactory track record; FATF- and DTAA-compliant jurisdiction; foreign applicant credit rating for last 3 years; fit-and-proper KMPs
regulation_content.effective_date: MGA references in sub-regulation (2) omitted w.e.f. 12 June 2026 (MGA Regulations, 2026)

The registration remains valid unless revoked or cancelled by the Authority.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Registration here is open-ended — it does not lapse on a fixed cycle but continues until revoked or cancelled. That places the weight on continuing compliance rather than periodic renewal.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Track and comply with any additional conditions attached to the certificate on an ongoing basis; there is no periodic renewal to prompt a review.

8.    If, after considering the application, the Authority is of the opinion that registration
      cannot be granted, it shall communicate the deficiencies to the Applicant giving it thirty
      days’ time to rectify them.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 8
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Where the Authority considers registration cannot be granted, it communicates the deficiencies to the applicant and gives thirty days to rectify them.
regulation_content.practical_point: Treat the deficiency letter as a hard thirty-day clock; triage the points immediately and route a complete, consolidated response rather than piecemeal replies.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Respond to a deficiency communication within thirty days with complete rectification; diarise the deadline.
regulation_content.risk_point: Letting the thirty-day window lapse, or responding partially, moves the application towards refusal under Regulation 9.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Thirty days to rectify deficiencies

regulation_content.regulation_text:
10.   An IIO registered with the Authority may carry any of the following class of businesses
      as may be permitted by the Authority subject to such conditions as may be specified: -

      (a)   Life Insurance Business;
      (b)   General Insurance Business;
      (c)   Health Insurance Business; or
      (d)   Re-insurance Business.

      Provided that the IIO registered as place of business of Indian Insurer or Branch Office
      of Foreign Insurer or Re-insurer shall be permitted to transact such class of business
      which is permitted to the Applicant by its home country regulatory or supervisory
      authority.

      [Provided further that at the time of making the application, the applicant shall opt for
      category as specified in clause (A) of sub-regulation (2) of Regulation 5 of the Insurance
      Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Re-insurance) Regulations, 2018, under
      which it intends to participate in reinsurance business emanating from the DTA]11
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 10
regulation_content.simple_explanation: An IIO may carry on life, general, health or re-insurance business as permitted by the Authority. An IIO that is a place of business of an Indian insurer, or a branch of a foreign insurer or re-insurer, may transact only the class its home regulator permits. At the application stage, a re-insurance applicant must opt for the category under Regulation 5(2)(A) of the IRDAI (Re-insurance) Regulations, 2018 under which it will participate in re-insurance emanating from the DTA.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The permitted class is tethered to the home-regulator's licence — an IIO cannot write in the IFSC a class it is not authorised to write at home. The IRDAI re-insurance category election, inserted by the 2024 amendment, matters because it fixes the IIO's order-of-preference position for DTA cessions.
regulation_content.practical_point: Map the classes sought to the home-regulator licence, and make the IRDAI re-insurance category election deliberately at application, since it governs DTA cession preference later.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Confirm the requested class is within the home-regulator authorisation; record the IRDAI re-insurance category opted for at application.
regulation_content.risk_point: Writing a class beyond the home-regulator's authorisation, or an ill-considered category election that weakens DTA cession preference, are the substantive exposures.
regulation_content.interview_point: You should be able to explain why an IIO's permissible classes are limited by its home-regulator licence, and what the IRDAI re-insurance category election affects.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Classes: life / general / health / re-insurance; class limited to home-regulator authorisation; IRDAI re-insurance category opted at application
regulation_content.effective_date: Re-insurance category proviso inserted by the 2024 Amendment

12.   An IIO shall not engage itself in any business other than for which the registration has
      been granted by the Authority.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 12
regulation_content.simple_explanation: An IIO must not engage in any business other than that for which registration has been granted.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is a hard perimeter around the registered activity — diversification into an unregistered line is a breach, not a commercial judgement call. Read it with Regulation 16, which is the route for adding related services.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Confirm any new activity falls within the registered scope; route genuinely new services through Regulation 16 prior approval.
regulation_content.risk_point: Straying beyond the registered class is a direct ground for action under Regulation 20.
regulation_content.important_numbers: No business beyond the registered scope

      the IFSC, from other SEZs and also from outside India.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 13

regulation_content.provision_heading: Restriction on direct insurance business from DTA
regulation_content.regulation_text:
14.   The IIO registered to transact direct insurance business shall not write direct insurance
      business from the DTA except in accordance with Section 2CB of the Insurance Act,
      1938.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 14
regulation_content.simple_explanation: An IIO registered for direct insurance must not write direct insurance business from the DTA except in accordance with Section 2CB of the Insurance Act, 1938.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is the line protecting the domestic market — DTA-sourced direct business is off-limits save through the narrow Section 2CB gateway. The geographic scope in Regulation 13 stops at the DTA border for direct business.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Screen the source of each direct-insurance risk; do not accept DTA-sourced direct business outside the Section 2CB route.
regulation_content.risk_point: Writing DTA direct business outside Section 2CB is a serious jurisdictional breach an inspection would treat gravely.
regulation_content.interview_point: A practical question: can a GIFT IFSC direct insurer write business sourced from mainland India, and on what basis?
regulation_content.important_numbers: No DTA direct insurance except under Section 2CB, Insurance Act 1938

regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 17 (source p.10)
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the continuing regulatory and governance requirements for an IIO across capital, solvency, governance and reporting. Key elements: NOF compliance under Section 6(3) of the Insurance Act, 1938 for a foreign re-insurance branch, maintained at all times; a minimum assigned capital equivalent to USD 1.5 million (earmarked and held in the home country) for an Indian insurer's place of business, a foreign insurer/re-insurer or Lloyd's branch; paid-up equity capital under Section 6(1) for public companies and the like; solvency margin as stipulated by the home regulator, with a quarterly Appointed Actuary certificate; commencement of business within twelve months of registration (extendable, on at least thirty days' advance application, to no more than eighteen months); appointment, with prior permission, of a Principal Officer and the required officers/KMPs who must be in direct employment and resident in India; books, KYC/AML, reporting in USD, and operational requirements; and prior approval for any change in shareholding exceeding five per cent of paid-up equity (prior intimation for changes below five per cent).
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This single regulation carries most of an IIO's continuing compliance load, and the obligations that bite hardest are the time-bound and threshold ones. The USD 1.5 million assigned capital and the solvency margin must be maintained at all times, not just demonstrated at registration; the twelve-month commencement clock, with its eighteen-month hard ceiling, cannot be cured by inaction; and the five per cent shareholding trigger catches ordinary corporate changes. The MGA-specific provisos throughout this regulation were omitted w.e.f. 12 June 2026.
regulation_content.practical_point: Build a continuing-compliance calendar off this regulation: rolling assigned-capital and solvency monitoring, the quarterly Appointed Actuary certificate, the twelve-month commencement deadline with a diarised thirty-day-advance extension trigger, and a shareholding-change control keyed to the five per cent threshold. Confirm all KMPs are in direct employment and India-resident.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain assigned capital of USD 1.5 million and the required solvency margin at all times; file the quarterly Appointed Actuary solvency certificate; commence business within twelve months (seek extension at least thirty days before expiry, capped at eighteen months); obtain prior approval for shareholding changes above five per cent and give prior intimation below it; report to the Authority in USD.
regulation_content.example: A foreign re-insurer's IIO that cannot commence business within twelve months must apply to the Chairperson at least thirty days before expiry; even then, no extension can run beyond eighteen months from the grant of registration. Separately, a 6% transfer of its parent-level IIO shareholding needs prior approval, while a 3% change needs only prior intimation.
regulation_content.risk_point: The recurring exposures are a lapse in maintained assigned capital or solvency between reporting dates, a missed quarterly actuary certificate, and letting the twelve-month commencement window pass without a timely extension application. A shareholding change slipped through without the five per cent analysis is a common corporate-secretarial miss.
regulation_content.interview_point: The interviewer may test the numbers under Regulation 17 — assigned capital, the commencement timeline and its outer limit, and the shareholding thresholds — and whether you understand these are continuing, at-all-times obligations rather than one-time registration conditions.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Assigned capital USD 1.5 million (at all times); solvency margin per home regulator + quarterly Appointed Actuary certificate; commence business within 12 months (extension >=30 days in advance; max 18 months); change in shareholding >5% prior approval, <5% prior intimation; reporting in USD
regulation_content.effective_date: MGA provisos omitted w.e.f. 12 June 2026 (MGA Regulations, 2026)

regulation_content.provision_heading: Power to specify procedures and issue clarification
regulation_content.regulation_text:
18.   Power to specify procedures and issue clarification:                 For the purpose of
      implementation of these Regulations and matter incidental thereto, or in order to facilitate
      and regulate financial services related to insurance and re-insurance in an IFSC, the
      Authority may specify such norms, procedures, processes, manners or provide
      clarification and relaxations, by way of guidelines or circulars, as it may deem fit.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 18
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Empowers the Authority to specify norms, procedures, processes and manners, and to issue clarifications and relaxations by guidelines or circulars, to implement the Regulations and regulate IFSC insurance activity.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Much of the operative detail for IIOs lives in circulars issued under this power rather than in the Regulations themselves, so compliance monitoring has to track IFSCA circulars, not just the base text.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Authority may issue guidelines/circulars and relaxations

regulation_content.regulation_text:
19.   Inspection, Investigation and Information: The Authority shall have the power to
      inspect and/or investigate the affairs of the IIO including calling for the information from
      the IIO, its employees and the Applicant, so far as it relates to its activities as an IIO.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 19
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Gives the Authority power to inspect and investigate the affairs of an IIO, including calling for information from the IIO, its employees and the applicant, so far as it relates to IIO activities.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Keep books, records and systems in an inspection-ready state; respond to information calls promptly and completely.
regulation_content.risk_point: Incomplete or delayed responses to an information call weigh against the IIO in any subsequent action under Regulation 20.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Authority's inspection, investigation and information powers

regulation_content.regulation_text:
20.   Action in case of Default:

      (1)   If pursuant to an inspection and/or investigation or otherwise, the Authority is of
            the opinion that the operations of an IIO are not being conducted in accordance
            with the provisions of the Act, rules or regulations made or circulars and guidelines
            issued thereunder or its activities are not in the interests of the insurance market or
            in the public interest, the Authority may take appropriate disciplinary action
            against it including but not limited to suspension or cancellation of certificate of
            registration, after giving an opportunity to the IIO of making its submissions.

      (2)   Without prejudice to the above, the Authority may take any other action as it deems
            fit, under the Act and other applicable laws.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 20
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Where, following inspection or otherwise, the Authority forms the opinion that an IIO's operations breach the Act, rules, regulations, circulars or guidelines, or are against the interests of the insurance market or the public, it may take disciplinary action — including suspension or cancellation of registration — after giving the IIO an opportunity to make submissions. It may also take any other action available under the Act and applicable laws.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Suspension or cancellation is the headline sanction, but the standard is broad — action can follow conduct 'not in the interests of the insurance market', which is wider than a specific rule breach. The opportunity-to-be-heard is the procedural check on that breadth.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Where action is proposed, ensure the opportunity to make submissions is used; maintain a documented compliance record that can rebut market-interest concerns.
regulation_content.risk_point: Because the trigger is broad, conduct that is technically compliant but market-damaging can still attract action; the defensive posture is a strong, evidenced compliance record.
regulation_content.interview_point: You should be able to state the range of actions available to the Authority on default and the due-process step that must precede them.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Suspension/cancellation of registration and other actions, after opportunity to be heard

regulation_content.regulation_text:
21.   Surrender of Certificate of Registration: An Applicant may be allowed to close its IIO
      and surrender its Certificate of registration only with the prior approval of the Authority
      and subject to such conditions as may be specified by the Authority.

regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Regulation 21 (source p.15)
regulation_content.simple_explanation: An applicant may close its IIO and surrender its certificate of registration only with the Authority's prior approval and subject to specified conditions.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Exit is not unilateral — surrender needs prior approval, which typically brings run-off and policyholder-protection conditions. Plan the wind-down around that approval rather than around a target closure date.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Seek prior approval before surrendering the certificate; anticipate run-off and liability-settlement conditions attached to approval.

regulation_content.regulation_text:
6.   Norms for establishing Service Companies of Lloyd’s IFSC: Managing Agents of
     Lloyd’s and companies registered under Companies Act, 2013 wishes to participate in
     Lloyd’s IFSC shall set up a service company with the following norms:

     (1)   The service company may be a private or a public company registered with
           Registrar of Companies in India, with a minimum paid up capital of INR five lakh;

     (2)   The main objects of Memorandum of Association and Article of Association shall
           be to provide all technical, underwriting, binding risks, settling claims,
           administrative, accounting, investment, regulatory and other assistance to the
           syndicate(s) whom they represent;

     (3)   The service company shall be responsible for all statutory & regulatory filings and
           compliances on behalf of the syndicate it represents;

     (4)   Any other requirement that may be specified by the Authority from time to time.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Second Schedule, Para 6 (source p.16)
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the norms for establishing a Service Company of Lloyd's IFSC — a private or public company registered in India with minimum paid-up capital of INR five lakh, with MoA/AoA objects covering technical, underwriting, claims, administrative and regulatory assistance to the syndicates it represents, and responsibility for the syndicate's statutory and regulatory filings.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Ensure the service company's paid-up capital and MoA/AoA objects meet the Second Schedule norms before registration.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Service Company minimum paid-up capital INR 5 lakh

regulation_content.chapter_title: Provisions applicable for Lloyd's and Lloyd's IFSC
regulation_content.provision_heading: Undertakings to be submitted by service company to Lloyd’s IFSC
regulation_content.regulation_text:
8.   Undertakings to be submitted by service company to Lloyd’s IFSC:

     (1)   The service company shall submit the Lloyd’s Service Company Coverholder
           Undertaking through which the Service Company agrees to comply with all
           relevant rules and requirements of Lloyd’s and the local legal, fiscal, taxation and
           regulatory authorities;

     (2)   The service company shall also submit the Lloyd’s Coverholder Decision Paper
           which provides detailed information on the proposed Service Company, including:
           (a) the level of underwriting and claims authority granted to the Service
                Company,
           (b) the business strategy for the Service Company,
           (c) details relating to principal staff operating in the Service Company,
           (d) financial information,
           (e) professional indemnity details,
           (f) classes of business to be underwritten by the Service Company,
           (g) the approach the Service Company will take to ensure compliance with
                registration requirements
           (h) other requirements as specified by Lloyd’s subject to approval of the
                Authority.

     (3)   Subsequent to submitting the decision paper, the service company shall perform
           Lloyd’s Service Company Self- Assessment against the Lloyd’s Minimum
           Standards which includes information such as any internal audit carried out on the
           Service Company;

     (4)   Any other requirement that may be specified by the Authority from time to time.
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Second Schedule, Para 8 (source p.16)
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires a service company to submit the Lloyd's Service Company Coverholder Undertaking, the Lloyd's Coverholder Decision Paper (covering underwriting/claims authority, strategy, staff, financials, indemnity and classes of business) and a self-assessment against the Lloyd's Minimum Standards.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Submit the Coverholder Undertaking, Decision Paper and Minimum-Standards self-assessment as part of onboarding.

regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the conditions governing service companies of Lloyd's IFSC — compliance with Lloyd's/Lloyd's IFSC conditions, the Service Company Underwriting Agreement delegating authority from syndicate members, responsibilities for binding insurances, premiums and claims, and the coverholder's obligations including prominent use of the syndicate name.

regulation_content.chapter_title: Provisions applicable for Lloyd's and Lloyd's IFSC
regulation_content.provision_heading: Cancellation of registration of Service Company
regulation_content.source_reference: IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021, Second Schedule, Para 10 (source p.21)
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Lets the Authority direct the administrator to cancel a service company's registration on specified grounds — including failure to commence business within twelve months of registration, ceasing to act as agent, failing a regulatory obligation, conduct detrimental to policyholders or the market, contravention of the Insurance Act 1938, conviction of a managerial officer, or furnishing false information.
regulation_content.risk_point: A service company that does not commence business within twelve months of registration is exposed to cancellation, mirroring the IIO commencement discipline.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Cancellation ground: no business within 12 months of registration, among others
